title: 2026-09-11 Research Notes — Axis, Eye, Door, Hysteresis and Constraint Dynamics
status: new project research extension; mathematical research notes, not validated physical theory
novelty_scope: Novel within the Tim Dooley / Potato of Life project research record on 2026-09-11. This is not a claim of global scientific priority for the underlying mathematics.

research_findings.finding: The existing Axis flow and Eye/observation map can be joined without pretending the observer sees the full state. If Phi_s is the Axis flow and o is an observable, define the observable evolution K^s o = o o Phi_s. This is the Koopman-operator viewpoint: nonlinear state dynamics can induce linear evolution on observables.
equations: K^s psi = exp(lambda s) psi for a Koopman eigenfunction psi
research_findings.project_consequence: Eye should be represented as a family of observables on Axis dynamics, not as access to the complete hidden state. Candidate coherent coordinates can be searched for in measured data rather than assumed in advance.
research_findings.test_path: For a chosen empirical domain, collect time/scale ordered observations, fit DMD/EDMD or another Koopman approximation, and compare out-of-sample prediction with a simpler autoregressive baseline.

research_findings.finding: A Door need not use one symmetric threshold. Many real transitions are path dependent. Give entry and exit different guards so crossing into a regime does not imply immediate reversal at the same value.
research_findings.project_consequence: This supplies a rigorous mathematical neighbor for threshold memory, residue and return-not-reset. It also separates a one-way initiation from a reversible gate.
research_findings.test_path: Estimate separate transition thresholds from repeated trajectories; compare a hysteretic model against a single-threshold model by predictive likelihood or held-out transition error.

research_findings.finding: Door events can be timestamped as first-passage or guard-crossing times rather than treated only as symbolic events.
equations: tau_k = inf{s>tau_(k-1) : h_k(X(s)) crosses its guard}
research_findings.project_consequence: A Ladder can become a sequence of measurable dwell intervals and transitions. This creates a bridge to survival analysis, renewal processes and hybrid systems.
research_findings.test_path: Measure dwell-time distributions and compare exponential, lognormal, Weibull and heavy-tail alternatives where data justify them.

research_findings.finding: The leash/cord relation is better represented first as a constraint set or coupling law, not as a new physical force. The same geometric constraint can describe support, tethering, covenant, control or captivity only after agency, direction and admissible control are specified.
equations: xdot = P_T_C(x) f(x) for projected feasible dynamics
M xddot = F(x,xdot)+J_g(x)^T lambda with g(x)=0 for a mechanical constrained system
research_findings.project_consequence: Moral or theological valence is not encoded by the multiplier lambda. It belongs in the objective, ownership/agency fields, consent state and consequences.
research_findings.test_path: For graph/control applications, compare outcomes when the constrained node controls release versus when another node exclusively controls release.

research_findings.finding: The existing viability-kernel Garden model gains a local safety quantity: distance to the non-viable boundary.
equations: robust cultivation seeks controls that keep m_V(x(t))>=m_min
research_findings.project_consequence: Garden becomes more than 'stay viable': it can measure how much room for disturbance remains before a critical boundary is reached.
research_findings.test_path: Use perturbation simulations or empirical stress events to estimate whether candidate controls increase minimum viability margin.

researcher_notes: The strongest new connection today is Axis→Eye through observable evolution. It gives the project a mathematically standard way to study hidden dynamics without claiming total observability.
Door hysteresis appears especially useful because several existing project ideas—residue, return, initiation, ash/mud/soil path dependence—already imply history dependence.
Constraint dynamics gives the leash language a precise home while preventing the archive from inventing a literal Leash Force.

external_science_sources.title: Modern Koopman Theory for Dynamical Systems

promotion_requirements: Choose a concrete empirical domain before assigning units.
Specify observables and baseline models before fitting.
Keep project theology separate from claims of physical mechanism.
Record parameter estimation and out-of-sample performance.
paper_subtitle: A research note translating Axis into hidden flow, Eye into observables, and Door into hysteretic threshold events with measurable crossing times.

paper_figures.title: Figure 1 · Axis, Eye and hysteretic Door
paper_figures.alt: A dynamics diagram showing hidden Axis flow, Eye observations, a Door with separate entry and exit thresholds, and measurable event timing.
paper_figures.caption: The model becomes testable when the Eye sees only declared observables, the Door has asymmetric entry/exit thresholds where path dependence is expected, and transition times can be compared against simpler threshold models.
paper_figures.source_note: Project research extension using hybrid systems, Koopman-observable and hysteresis mathematics.

reader_takeaway: The Eye is more rigorous as an observation operator than as access to the complete hidden state.
A Door can remember direction when entry and exit thresholds differ; that is ordinary hysteresis, not mystical irreversibility.
Door events can be measured through first-passage times and dwell intervals.
Hysteresis only earns retention if repeated trajectories predict better than a simpler single-threshold model.

equation_context.role: Observable hybrid-dynamics note. Axis is treated as hidden flow, Eye as a measurement operator and Door as a threshold/reset with possible hysteresis.

variables.Φ_s: Flow map evolving X along parameter s.
variables.τ_down: Exit threshold, lower than τ_up when hysteresis is present.
variables.τ_k: First crossing/event time for a declared guard.

equation_context.units_and_types: Thresholds and h(X) must share compatible units or be normalized dimensionlessly. Event times inherit the units of the evolution parameter.
equation_context.observable_consequence: Repeated trajectories should show asymmetric entry/exit thresholds or improved transition-time prediction relative to a single-threshold model.
equation_context.boundary: Hysteresis is ordinary path dependence; it should not be interpreted as mystical irreversibility without additional evidence.

failure_conditions: A single-threshold model predicts held-out transitions as well as the hysteretic model.
Estimated entry and exit thresholds are not distinguishable within uncertainty.
Transition timing cannot be reproduced across repeated trajectories or sessions.
The proposed Eye observable is not measurable or does not track the hidden-state distinction the model assumes.
